# Installation

Lynx Kit components are published to npm under the `@lynx-kit` scope. Each component is its own
package, so you add only the ones you need.

## Requirements

- A Lynx app created with Rspeedy (`@lynx-js/rspeedy`) and ReactLynx (`@lynx-js/react`)
- `@lynx-js/react` 0.100.0 or newer
- `@lynx-js/types` 4 or newer
- `@types/react` 19 or newer

## Install the package


```sh [npm]
npm install @lynx-kit/modal
```

```sh [yarn]
yarn add @lynx-kit/modal
```

```sh [pnpm]
pnpm add @lynx-kit/modal
```

```sh [bun]
bun add @lynx-kit/modal
```

```sh [deno]
deno add npm:@lynx-kit/modal
```

## Compile the package source

The package ships JSX (`.jsx` files) so that ReactLynx can compile it for the main thread and the
background thread. Bundlers skip `node_modules` by default, so tell Rspeedy to include the package.
Add a `source.include` entry to `lynx.config.ts`:

```ts title="lynx.config.ts"
import { defineConfig } from '@lynx-js/rspeedy';
import { pluginQRCode } from '@lynx-js/qrcode-rsbuild-plugin';
import { pluginReactLynx } from '@lynx-js/react-rsbuild-plugin';

export default defineConfig({
  source: {
    include: [/@lynx-kit/],
  },
  plugins: [pluginQRCode(), pluginReactLynx()],
});
```

Keep the plugins your project already has and only add the `source` block. Restart the dev server
after editing the config.

:::tip
Without this entry you will see a JSX syntax error that points into
`node_modules/@lynx-kit/modal`.
:::

## Tailwind is optional

The modal ships its own precompiled CSS, so your app does not need Tailwind. If your app does use
Tailwind, see [Styling and Theming](/docs/guide/styling.md) to learn how to combine them.

## Next step

Continue with the [Quick Start](/docs/guide/get-started/quick-start.md).

# API overview

## Components

| Package           | Component                    | Description                                                                                     |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `@lynx-kit/modal` | [Modal](/docs/apis/modal.md) | A customizable, animated modal dialog with title, description, icon, custom content and actions |

## Conventions

These rules apply to every Lynx Kit component.

| Convention | Details                                                                                                       |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Controlled | State such as `visible` is owned by your code. Components call your callbacks and never change it themselves. |
| Events     | Lynx event names are used: `bindtap` and `catchtap`, not `onClick`.                                           |
| Colors     | Color props such as `accentColor` take any CSS color and are applied inline.                                  |
| Classes    | `className` props extend the defaults. Library classes use the `lk-` prefix.                                  |
| Types      | Every package ships `.d.ts` files and exports its props type, for example `ModalProps`.                       |

> For AI agents: the complete documentation index is available at /docs/llms.txt, the full documentation bundle is available at /docs/llms-full.txt.

# Modal

A customizable, animated modal dialog for Lynx apps. Package: `@lynx-kit/modal`.

## Install


```sh [npm]
npm install @lynx-kit/modal
```

```sh [yarn]
yarn add @lynx-kit/modal
```

```sh [pnpm]
pnpm add @lynx-kit/modal
```

```sh [bun]
bun add @lynx-kit/modal
```

```sh [deno]
deno add npm:@lynx-kit/modal
```

Add the package to `source.include` in `lynx.config.ts`. See
[Installation](/docs/guide/get-started/installation.md#compile-the-package-source).

## Import

```ts
import { Modal } from '@lynx-kit/modal';
import type { ModalProps } from '@lynx-kit/modal';
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { useState } from '@lynx-js/react';
import { Modal } from '@lynx-kit/modal';

export function Example() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

  return (
    <view>
      <view bindtap={() => setOpen(true)}>
        <text>Show modal</text>
      </view>

      <Modal
        visible={open}
        onClose={() => setOpen(false)}
        title="Delete project?"
        description="This action can't be undone."
        confirmText="Delete"
        accentColor="#ef4444"
        onConfirm={() => setOpen(false)}
      />
    </view>
  );
}
```

## Props

### Content

| Prop          | Type        | Default | Description                                                               |
| ------------- | ----------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `title`       | `string`    | none    | Heading text, centered below the icon                                     |
| `description` | `string`    | none    | Supporting text under the title                                           |
| `icon`        | `ReactNode` | none    | Rendered inside a circular badge at the top. The badge uses `accentColor` |
| `children`    | `ReactNode` | none    | Custom content, rendered between the description and the actions          |

### State and events

| Prop                | Type         | Default  | Description                                                               |
| ------------------- | ------------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `visible`           | `boolean`    | required | Whether the modal is open                                                 |
| `onClose`           | `() => void` | required | Called when the cancel button or the backdrop is tapped                   |
| `onConfirm`         | `() => void` | none     | Called when the confirm button is tapped. It does **not** close the modal |
| `closeOnOverlayTap` | `boolean`    | `true`   | Set to `false` to ignore taps on the backdrop                             |

### Actions

| Prop          | Type        | Default    | Description                                                           |
| ------------- | ----------- | ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `confirmText` | `string`    | none       | Label of the confirm button. The button only renders when this is set |
| `cancelText`  | `string`    | `'Cancel'` | Label of the cancel button                                            |
| `footer`      | `ReactNode` | none       | Replaces the default action buttons entirely                          |

### Appearance

| Prop               | Type     | Default                    | Description                                                        |
| ------------------ | -------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `accentColor`      | `string` | indigo (`bg-indigo-500`)   | Background of the icon badge and the confirm button. Any CSS color |
| `surfaceColor`     | `string` | white (`bg-white`)         | Background of the card. Any CSS color                              |
| `overlayColor`     | `string` | `'rgba(10, 12, 24, 0.55)'` | Backdrop color while the modal is open. Any CSS color              |
| `className`        | `string` | `''`                       | Extra classes for the card                                         |
| `overlayClassName` | `string` | `''`                       | Extra classes for the backdrop                                     |

## Type definition

```ts
export interface ModalProps {
  visible: boolean;
  onClose: () => void;
  title?: string;
  description?: string;
  icon?: ReactNode;
  children?: ReactNode;
  confirmText?: string;
  cancelText?: string;
  onConfirm?: () => void;
  footer?: ReactNode;
  closeOnOverlayTap?: boolean;
  accentColor?: string;
  surfaceColor?: string;
  overlayColor?: string;
  className?: string;
  overlayClassName?: string;
}
```

## Behavior

- **Controlled.** You own `visible`. The modal never opens or closes by itself.
- **Animation.** On open, the backdrop fades in and the card fades and scales in over 240 ms. On
  close, the same transition plays in reverse, and the modal unmounts after it finishes.
- **Backdrop.** A tap on the backdrop calls `onClose` unless `closeOnOverlayTap` is `false`. Taps on
  the card do not reach the backdrop.
- **Placement.** The backdrop is positioned over its parent with `z-index: 1000`. Lynx has no portals,
  so render `<Modal>` at the root of your page.
- **Size.** The card is 5/6 of the width, up to a maximum of 360 px.

## Examples

### Confirmation dialog

```tsx
<Modal
  visible={open}
  onClose={() => setOpen(false)}
  title="Discard changes?"
  description="Your edits will be lost."
  confirmText="Discard"
  cancelText="Keep editing"
  accentColor="#ef4444"
  onConfirm={() => {
    discard();
    setOpen(false);
  }}
/>
```

### Information only (no confirm button)

Leave out `confirmText` and only the cancel button renders. Use `cancelText` to relabel it:

```tsx
<Modal
  visible={open}
  onClose={() => setOpen(false)}
  title="Update available"
  description="Restart the app to finish updating."
  cancelText="Got it"
/>
```

### Icon and custom content

```tsx
<Modal
  visible={open}
  onClose={() => setOpen(false)}
  icon={<text style={{ color: '#ffffff', fontSize: '24px' }}>!</text>}
  title="Low storage"
  confirmText="Manage"
  onConfirm={openSettings}
>
  <text>Free up space to keep syncing your photos.</text>
</Modal>
```

### Custom footer

`footer` replaces the default buttons, so you can build any layout:

```tsx
<Modal
  visible={open}
  onClose={() => setOpen(false)}
  title="Rate this app"
  footer={
    <view style={{ marginTop: '24px', width: '100%' }} bindtap={() => setOpen(false)}>
      <text style={{ textAlign: 'center' }}>Maybe later</text>
    </view>
  }
/>
```

### Block backdrop dismissal

```tsx
<Modal
  visible={open}
  onClose={() => setOpen(false)}
  closeOnOverlayTap={false}
  title="Processing"
  description="Please wait."
/>
```

### Theme it

```tsx
<Modal
  visible={open}
  onClose={() => setOpen(false)}
  title="Dark mode"
  surfaceColor="#0f172a"
  overlayColor="rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.75)"
  accentColor="#22d3ee"
  confirmText="Enable"
/>
```

## Notes

- The default title, description and button text colors are fixed (slate and white), so pick a
  `surfaceColor` that keeps them readable, or provide your own `footer` and `children`.
- `className` classes such as `!bg-red-500` come from your app's Tailwind build. If your app does not
  use Tailwind, use the color props.

# Creating a component

This guide shows how `@lynx-kit/modal` was built, so you can add the next component to the kit
(a bottom sheet, a toast and so on) the same way. Every component is its own package in a pnpm
workspace, with a playground app to try it in.

## Workspace layout

```text
lynx-kit/
├─ package.json
├─ pnpm-workspace.yaml
├─ .changeset/
├─ packages/
│  └─ modal/          -> @lynx-kit/modal
└─ apps/
   ├─ playground/     -> an Rspeedy app used to try components
   └─ docs/           -> this website
```


### Create the workspace
```bash
mkdir lynx-kit && cd lynx-kit
pnpm init
mkdir packages apps
```
```yaml title="pnpm-workspace.yaml"
packages:
  - 'packages/*'
  - 'apps/*'
```
```json title="package.json (root)"
{
  "private": true,
  "scripts": {
    "build": "pnpm -r --filter './packages/*' build",
    "release": "pnpm build && changeset publish"
  }
}
```
```bash
pnpm add -Dw @changesets/cli && pnpm changeset init
```
In `.changeset/config.json`, set `"access": "public"`.
### Scaffold the library package
```bash
pnpm create @lynx-js/lynx@latest packages/modal --template rslib-react-ts
```
The template creates a Rslib project with a `Counter` example. Keep its `rslib.config.ts`: it must
keep `target: "web"`, preserve JSX and build in bundleless mode (`bundle: false`), so that `dist/`
keeps `import './styles.css'` and emits the CSS next to the JavaScript.
### Name the package
The template names the package after its folder (`modal`). pnpm links workspace packages by the
`name` field, so change it to the scoped name:
```json title="packages/modal/package.json"
{
  "name": "@lynx-kit/modal",
  "version": "0.1.0"
}
```
### Set up Tailwind v3 with a prefix
```bash
cd packages/modal
pnpm add -D tailwindcss@^3 @lynx-js/tailwind-preset
```
```js title="packages/modal/tailwind.config.mjs"
import lynxPreset from '@lynx-js/tailwind-preset';

export default {
  prefix: 'lk-',
  content: ['./src/**/*.{ts,tsx}'],
  presets: [lynxPreset],
};
```
```js title="packages/modal/postcss.config.mjs"
export default { plugins: { tailwindcss: {} } };
```
```css title="packages/modal/src/styles.css"
@tailwind base;
@tailwind utilities;
```
The library runs Tailwind at build time, so apps do not need to scan `node_modules` for class names.
The `lk-` prefix keeps the library's classes from clashing with the app's own.
### Write the component
Create `src/Modal.tsx`. Layout, color and typography come from `lk-` classes. Animation values live
in inline styles because they depend on state.
```tsx title="packages/modal/src/Modal.tsx"
import { useEffect, useState } from '@lynx-js/react';
import type { ReactNode } from '@lynx-js/react';
import './styles.css';

const DURATION = 240;

function usePresence(visible: boolean) {
  const [mounted, setMounted] = useState(visible);
  const [shown, setShown] = useState(false);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (visible) {
      setMounted(true);
      const t = setTimeout(() => setShown(true), 16);
      return () => clearTimeout(t);
    }
    setShown(false);
    const t = setTimeout(() => setMounted(false), DURATION);
    return () => clearTimeout(t);
  }, [visible]);

  return { mounted, shown };
}

export interface ModalProps {
  visible: boolean;
  onClose: () => void;
  title?: string;
  description?: string;
  icon?: ReactNode;
  children?: ReactNode;
  confirmText?: string;
  cancelText?: string;
  onConfirm?: () => void;
  footer?: ReactNode;
  closeOnOverlayTap?: boolean;
  accentColor?: string;
  surfaceColor?: string;
  overlayColor?: string;
  className?: string;
  overlayClassName?: string;
}

export function Modal({
  visible,
  onClose,
  title,
  description,
  icon,
  children,
  confirmText,
  cancelText = 'Cancel',
  onConfirm,
  footer,
  closeOnOverlayTap = true,
  accentColor,
  surfaceColor,
  overlayColor = 'rgba(10, 12, 24, 0.55)',
  className = '',
  overlayClassName = '',
}: ModalProps) {
  const { mounted, shown } = usePresence(visible);
  if (!mounted) return null;

  const accent = accentColor ? { backgroundColor: accentColor } : undefined;

  return (
    <view
      className={`lk-fixed lk-top-0 lk-left-0 lk-right-0 lk-bottom-0 lk-flex lk-flex-col lk-items-center lk-justify-center ${overlayClassName}`}
      style={{
        zIndex: 1000,
        backgroundColor: shown ? overlayColor : 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)',
        transition: `background-color ${DURATION}ms ease`,
      }}
      bindtap={() => closeOnOverlayTap && onClose()}
    >
      <view
        className={`lk-flex lk-flex-col lk-items-center lk-w-5/6 lk-px-6 lk-pt-7 lk-pb-5 lk-bg-white lk-rounded-3xl ${className}`}
        style={{
          maxWidth: '360px',
          ...(surfaceColor ? { backgroundColor: surfaceColor } : null),
          opacity: shown ? 1 : 0,
          transform: shown ? 'scale(1) translateY(0px)' : 'scale(0.92) translateY(16px)',
          transition: `opacity ${DURATION}ms ease, transform ${DURATION}ms ease`,
          boxShadow: '0 24px 60px rgba(10, 12, 24, 0.28)',
        }}
        catchtap={() => {}}
      >
        {icon && (
          <view
            className="lk-flex lk-items-center lk-justify-center lk-w-14 lk-h-14 lk-mb-4 lk-rounded-full lk-bg-indigo-500"
            style={accent}
          >
            {icon}
          </view>
        )}

        {title && (
          <text className="lk-text-xl lk-font-bold lk-text-center lk-text-slate-900">{title}</text>
        )}

        {description && (
          <text className="lk-mt-2 lk-text-sm lk-text-center lk-text-slate-500">{description}</text>
        )}

        {children && <view className="lk-w-full lk-mt-4">{children}</view>}

        {footer ?? (
          <view className="lk-flex lk-flex-row lk-gap-3 lk-w-full lk-mt-6">
            <view
              className="lk-flex lk-flex-1 lk-items-center lk-justify-center lk-h-12 lk-rounded-2xl lk-bg-slate-100"
              bindtap={onClose}
            >
              <text className="lk-text-base lk-font-semibold lk-text-slate-800">{cancelText}</text>
            </view>

            {confirmText && (
              <view
                className="lk-flex lk-flex-1 lk-items-center lk-justify-center lk-h-12 lk-rounded-2xl lk-bg-indigo-500"
                style={accent}
                bindtap={onConfirm}
              >
                <text className="lk-text-base lk-font-semibold lk-text-white">{confirmText}</text>
              </view>
            )}
          </view>
        )}
      </view>
    </view>
  );
}
```
Design notes:
- `usePresence` keeps the element mounted for `DURATION` after `visible` becomes `false`, so the exit
  animation can play. The 16 ms delay on enter lets the first frame render at the start values.
- The backdrop handles `bindtap` to close. The card uses `catchtap`, which stops the tap from
  bubbling to the backdrop.
- `onConfirm` does not close the modal. The parent owns the state, which is the more predictable
  controlled pattern.
### Export it
Use extensionless relative imports. The build keeps JSX, so the output files are `.jsx`, and a `.js`
extension in the import would point to a file that does not exist.
```ts title="packages/modal/src/index.ts"
export type { ModalProps } from './Modal';
export { Modal } from './Modal';
```
### Point the package at its output
Build once and look at what `dist` contains:
```bash
pnpm --filter "@lynx-kit/modal" build
```
With JSX preserved you get `index.jsx`, `Modal.jsx`, `styles.css` and the `.d.ts` files, so the entry
points must name `.jsx`:
```json title="packages/modal/package.json"
{
  "name": "@lynx-kit/modal",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "description": "A customizable modal for Lynx apps, styled with Tailwind.",
  "license": "MIT",
  "keywords": ["lynx", "lynxjs", "reactlynx", "modal", "tailwindcss", "ui"],
  "type": "module",
  "sideEffects": ["**/*.css"],
  "main": "./dist/index.jsx",
  "types": "./dist/index.d.ts",
  "exports": {
    ".": {
      "types": "./dist/index.d.ts",
      "import": "./dist/index.jsx",
      "default": "./dist/index.jsx"
    },
    "./package.json": "./package.json"
  },
  "files": ["dist", "README.md"],
  "publishConfig": { "access": "public" },
  "scripts": {
    "build": "rslib build",
    "dev": "rslib build --watch",
    "prepublishOnly": "pnpm build"
  },
  "peerDependencies": {
    "@lynx-js/react": ">=0.100.0",
    "@lynx-js/types": ">=4",
    "@types/react": ">=19"
  }
}
```
Keep the template's `devDependencies`. The `default` condition matters: Rspeedy builds an app twice
(a background layer and a main-thread layer), and an `exports` map with only `import` can fail to
resolve in one of them.
After the build, confirm that `dist/` contains a `.css` file with `lk-` classes and that the built
component still imports it.
### Try it in the playground
```bash
cd apps/playground
pnpm add @lynx-kit/modal --workspace
cd ../..
pnpm --filter "@lynx-kit/modal" build
pnpm --filter playground dev
```
The playground imports `dist/`, which does not update until you rebuild. Run
`pnpm --filter "@lynx-kit/modal" dev` in a second terminal for a watcher.
Start with the template's `Counter` to prove that the wiring works, then swap the export to `Modal`.

## Growing the kit

- **More components.** Add `packages/bottom-sheet`, `packages/toast` and so on, each published as
  `@lynx-kit/<name>`. When two packages share code such as `usePresence`, move it into
  `@lynx-kit/core`.
- **Starter app.** A future unscoped `create-lynx-kit` package could scaffold an Rspeedy app with
  Tailwind v3, the Lynx preset, PostCSS and `source.include` already configured.
- **Design tokens.** A shared `@lynx-kit/tailwind-preset` can hold brand colors and radii once there
  is more than one component.

Next, learn how to [publish to npm](/docs/guide/publishing.md).

# Quick start

Show your first modal in a few minutes.


### Install and configure
Follow [Installation](/docs/guide/get-started/installation.md) to add `@lynx-kit/modal` and the
`source.include` entry.
### Add the modal to a page
Keep the open state in your component and render `<Modal>` at the root of the page:
```tsx title="src/App.tsx"
import { useState } from '@lynx-js/react';
import { Modal } from '@lynx-kit/modal';

export function App() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

  return (
    <view
      style={{
        display: 'flex',
        flexDirection: 'column',
        flex: 1,
        alignItems: 'center',
        justifyContent: 'center',
      }}
    >
      <view
        style={{ padding: '12px 24px', borderRadius: '16px', backgroundColor: '#6366f1' }}
        bindtap={() => setOpen(true)}
      >
        <text style={{ color: '#ffffff' }}>Show modal</text>
      </view>

      <Modal
        visible={open}
        onClose={() => setOpen(false)}
        title="Delete project?"
        description="This action can't be undone."
        confirmText="Delete"
        accentColor="#ef4444"
        onConfirm={() => setOpen(false)}
      />
    </view>
  );
}
```
### Run it
```bash
pnpm dev
```
Scan the QR code with Lynx Explorer and tap the button.

## Things to know

- **Controlled component.** `onConfirm` does not close the modal. Your code decides what happens, and
  you close it by setting `visible` to `false`.
- **Tap handlers.** Lynx uses `bindtap`, not `onClick`.
- **Render at the page root.** Lynx has no portals, so the overlay covers whichever view it is
  rendered in. Place `<Modal>` near the top of your page component.
- **Layout.** A Lynx `view` uses a linear layout by default, so set `display: 'flex'` when you
  want `align-items` to apply. See [Troubleshooting](/docs/guide/troubleshooting.md).

Next, read the full [Modal API](/docs/apis/modal.md).

# Publishing to npm

How to publish a package from the workspace to the `@lynx-kit` scope.

## Before the first publish

- `src/index.ts` exports the component you are shipping.
- `packages/<name>/README.md` has the install command, a props table and a usage example.
- `packages/<name>/LICENSE` contains the MIT license text. Without it the package declares a license
  it does not include.
- `pnpm --filter "@lynx-kit/<name>" build` succeeds and `dist/` contains the `.jsx`, `.d.ts` and
  `.css` files.

## Publish


### Turn on two-factor authentication
npm requires 2FA for publishing. On npmjs.com open **Account**, then **Two-Factor Authentication**,
and enable it with the **Authorization and publishing** level. Without it, the registry answers with
a `403 Forbidden` and never asks for a one-time code.
### Log in and confirm ownership
Run these from your home folder, not from the repository. The repository declares pnpm as its package
manager, so npm refuses to run inside it (`EBADDEVENGINES`).
```bash
cd ~
npm login
npm whoami
npm org ls lynx-kit
```
You should appear in the list with the `owner` role.
### Inspect what will ship
```bash
cd packages/modal
pnpm build
pnpm publish --dry-run --no-git-checks
```
The tarball should contain only `dist/`, `package.json`, `README.md` and `LICENSE`.
### Publish
```bash
npm publish --access public
```
npm opens a browser prompt (or asks for a one-time code). Scoped packages default to private, so
`--access public` is required. The `publishConfig` in `package.json` already sets it.
### Verify
```bash
cd ~
npm view @lynx-kit/modal
```
Then install it in a fresh Rspeedy app outside the monorepo and render it.

## Releasing a new version

Versions are permanent. You cannot republish a version number, so bump it first:

```bash
pnpm changeset          # pick the package, choose major, minor or patch, write a summary
pnpm changeset version  # bumps the version and writes CHANGELOG.md
```

Then publish again from the package folder.

## Giving your team access

After the first publish, open the organization's **Teams** page on npmjs.com, add the package to a
team and choose read-only or read/write. The package list stays empty until a package exists.

## Publishing from CI

npm is restricting tokens that bypass 2FA for direct publishing. When you automate releases, use
npm's trusted publishing (OIDC) from GitHub Actions instead of a long-lived token.

## Test the tarball before you publish

```bash
cd packages/modal
pnpm pack
```

In a fresh Rspeedy app run `pnpm add path/to/lynx-kit-modal-0.1.0.tgz`. If you hit a JSX error, add
`source.include` as described in [Installation](/docs/guide/get-started/installation.md).

> For AI agents: the complete documentation index is available at /docs/llms.txt, the full documentation bundle is available at /docs/llms-full.txt.

# Styling and theming

Lynx Kit components are styled with Tailwind CSS v3, compiled when the library is built. That has
three consequences for you:

1. Your app does **not** need Tailwind for the components to look right.
2. Every class inside the library starts with `lk-`, for example `lk-bg-white`, so the library
   cannot clash with your own classes.
3. There are no CSS variables to configure in the host app.

## Change colors with props

The quickest way to theme a component is through its color props. They accept any CSS color and are
applied inline:

```tsx
<Modal
  visible={open}
  onClose={() => setOpen(false)}
  title="Sign out?"
  confirmText="Sign out"
  accentColor="#0ea5e9"
  surfaceColor="#0f172a"
  overlayColor="rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.7)"
/>
```

| Prop           | What it changes                       |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `accentColor`  | The icon badge and the confirm button |
| `surfaceColor` | The card background                   |
| `overlayColor` | The dimmed backdrop                   |

## Extend with classes

Every component accepts `className` for the card and `overlayClassName` for the backdrop. These
classes are added after the defaults.

If your app uses Tailwind v3, use the `!` (important) modifier to win over a default:

```tsx
<Modal className="!bg-slate-900" overlayClassName="!bg-black/80" visible={open} onClose={close} />
```

Those classes are generated by **your** Tailwind build, not the library's, so the app must have
Tailwind configured. Otherwise, use the color props above.

## Using Tailwind in your own Lynx app

Lynx currently requires Tailwind CSS v3. The v4 packages are not compatible with
`@lynx-js/tailwind-preset`, which removes the utilities Lynx does not support and swaps in
Lynx-specific alternatives. The preset is still marked unstable.

```bash
pnpm add -D tailwindcss@^3 @lynx-js/tailwind-preset
```

```js title="postcss.config.mjs"
export default { plugins: { tailwindcss: {} } };
```

```js title="tailwind.config.mjs"
import lynxPreset from '@lynx-js/tailwind-preset';

export default {
  content: ['./src/**/*.{js,ts,jsx,tsx}'],
  presets: [lynxPreset],
};
```

```css title="src/App.css"
@tailwind base;
@tailwind utilities;
```

## Animation

Animation values (opacity, scale, translate and duration) are inline styles, because they change with
state and not every Tailwind transition or transform utility is supported by the Lynx preset.

# Troubleshooting

## JSX syntax error from `node_modules/@lynx-kit/modal`

The package ships `.jsx` files and bundlers skip `node_modules` by default. Add the package to
`source.include` in your `lynx.config.ts`, then restart the dev server:

```ts
export default defineConfig({
  source: { include: [/@lynx-kit/] },
  // ...
});
```

## Items are not centered

A Lynx `view` defaults to `display: linear`, where `justify-content` works but `align-items` is
ignored. Set the display mode explicitly:

```tsx
<view
  style={{
    display: 'flex',
    flexDirection: 'column',
    flex: 1,
    alignItems: 'center',
    justifyContent: 'center',
  }}
>
```

If the view does not fill the screen, give the root element a defined size, since `flex: 1` needs a
sized parent.

## The modal does not close

`onConfirm` never closes the modal. Set `visible` to `false` in your handler:

```tsx
onConfirm={() => {
  save();
  setOpen(false);
}}
```

## Click handlers do nothing

Lynx uses `bindtap` and `catchtap`, not `onClick`.

## The modal is hidden behind other content

Lynx has no portals. Render `<Modal>` at the root of the page, not inside a scroll view or a
clipped container.

## `Can't resolve '@lynx-kit/modal'` in a monorepo

When you develop the library inside a pnpm workspace, check these in order:

1. The `name` field in `packages/modal/package.json` must be exactly `@lynx-kit/modal`. Run
   `pnpm ls -r --depth -1` to see the names pnpm uses.
2. The playground must depend on it: `"@lynx-kit/modal": "workspace:*"`.
3. Build output decides the entry. Check `dist` and make sure `main`, `types` and `exports` point at
   files that exist. See [Creating a component](/docs/guide/creating-a-component.md).
4. Restart the dev server after changing `package.json`, since resolution failures are cached.

## `npm` commands fail with `EBADDEVENGINES`

The repository declares pnpm as its package manager, so npm refuses to run inside it. Run `npm login`
and `npm org ls` from your home folder, and use `pnpm` for everything inside the repository.

# Alpha Version

UI components for Lynx apps

> Customizable, animated and typed. Install one package and use it.

[Get Started](/guide/get-started/installation) | [API Reference](/apis/modal)

## Features

- /icons/icon-lynx-native.svg **Built for Lynx**: Written with Lynx elements and events (view, text, bindtap), so it renders natively on Android and iOS.
- /icons/icon-tailwind.svg **Tailwind, precompiled**: Styled with Tailwind v3 at build time. Your app does not need Tailwind, and every class uses an lk- prefix so nothing clashes.
- /icons/icon-controlled.svg **Controlled API**: You own the state. Pass visible and onClose, and the component never surprises you.
- /icons/icon-colors.svg **Easy to theme**: Override the accent, surface and overlay colors with plain props, or extend the classes.
- /icons/icon-typed.svg **Typed**: Ships TypeScript declarations, so props autocomplete in your editor.
- /icons/icon-animated.svg **Animated**: Enter and exit transitions are built in, driven by a small presence hook.
